title: Inspector Thorne
paragraphs: A short-run detective drama produced by Frank and Anne Hummert, centered on Inspector Thorne's investigations of murder and other serious crimes.

Short NBC sustaining detective series created by Frank and Anne Hummert. Frozen GRH set preserves broadcasts 1-10 of the eleven-show run; Society Writer Murder Case, September 27, 1951, is the only documented final broadcast not represented.

GRH documents the program through Karl Weber lead era (July 20, 1951 to August 31, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Staats Cotsworth lead era (September 6, 1951 to September 27, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Dan Ocko (performer on 10 recordings), Frank Hummert (creator on 9 recordings and author on 1 recording), Fred Collins (announcer on 10 recordings), Anne Hummert (creator on 7 recordings and author on 1 recording), [[person|karl-weber|Karl Weber]] (performer on 7 recordings), Edward Slattery (director on 5 recordings), and Kenneth MacGregor (director on 5 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include police homicide investigation, murder mystery, witness interrogation and clue analysis, NBC sustaining crime drama, and urban crime and social motives.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Eleven-broadcast Inspector Thorne run, Lead transition from Karl Weber to Staats Cotsworth, September move from Friday to Thursday, and Inspector Thorne NBC launch.
